Trump’s Nvidia Rescue Could Trigger a Political Firestorm on Capitol Hill


Trump’s personal intervention in Nvidia’s leadership crisis may have given the company a way forward — but it could also open the door to a much bigger fight in Washington.

Trump reportedly played a direct role in bringing CEO Jensen Huang back to the helm of the semiconductor giant. The president later acknowledged that he had spoken with Nvidia’s board and helped persuade directors to reverse course.

What may have looked like a business decision is quickly becoming a political and national security issue.

Nvidia was already facing growing scrutiny over Huang’s personal connections and allegations involving possible Chinese espionage. The company’s position is particularly sensitive because its advanced AI chips sit at the center of the escalating technology competition between Washington and Beijing.

Now lawmakers want answers. Congressional investigators are expected to examine why senior administration officials became involved in a private company's leadership decisions, what assurances were given to Nvidia’s board, and whether national security concerns were adequately addressed.

The controversy could become especially uncomfortable for the White House as Democrats prepare to take control of key congressional committees in January. Several lawmakers have already signaled plans to investigate the administration’s role in the episode.

Huang is also expected to face questions from lawmakers, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick could come under renewed scrutiny over the government's handling of sensitive technology exports.

For Nvidia, the immediate challenge is no longer simply restoring confidence in its leadership. The company must also convince Washington that its business decisions, particularly those involving China, will not undermine US security interests.

Trump may have helped bring Huang back. But the political consequences of that decision could follow Nvidia for months — and potentially put the administration itself under the congressional spotlight.

📄 Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Predicted lineups, team news, and stats

📌 Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Get the predicted lineups, injury updates, team news, kick-off times and key statistics ahead of the clash.

Arsenal welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium in Matchday 5 of the UEFA Champions League, with Mikel Arteta's side looking to preserve their unbeaten European campaign. The Gunners face a selection headache, however, with David Raya expected to miss out and Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi unavailable through injury.
​
Dortmund arrive in London on an eight-match unbeaten run in all competitions and sit just one point behind Arsenal in the Champions League standings. The hosts could also move a step closer to two significant European records with victory over the Bundesliga leaders.
​
Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to replace Raya in goal for Arsenal, while Dortmund's attacking selection could depend on the fitness of Serhou Guirassy.
​
Arsenal predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Kepa Arrizabalaga; Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel, Piero Hincapié; Myles Lewis-Skelly, Declan Rice; Noni Madueke, Martin Ødegaard, Eberechi Eze; Viktor Gyökeres.
​
Borussia Dortmund predicted XI (3-4-2-1): Gregor Kobel; Nico Schlotterbeck, Waldemar Anton, Ramy Bensebaini; Julian Ryerson, Felix Nmecha, Jobe Bellingham, Daniel Svensson; Konstantinos Karetsas, Maximilian Beier; Fábio Silva.
​
Alternative predicted selections include Bruno Guimarães and Mikel Merino for Arsenal, while Joey Veerman could feature in Dortmund's midfield. Neither starting XI has been confirmed.
​
David Raya was forced off during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle United following a collision with Will Osula. Arteta indicated that the goalkeeper would not require surgery, although the full extent of his injury remains unclear. Kepa is expected to deputise against Dortmund.
​
Bukayo Saka faces another four weeks on the sidelines, while Martín Zubimendi is unavailable with a hamstring injury. There is more encouraging news regarding William Saliba, who could feature as he continues his recovery from a long-term back injury.
​
Niko Kovac has fitness concerns surrounding Serhou Guirassy after the striker suffered a hamstring problem against Real Betis. Carney Chukwuemeka is also doubtful with a muscle injury.
​
Emre Can, Giannis Konstantelias and Samuele Inácio are unavailable, while Justin Lerma's participation remains uncertain.
​
Arsenal occupy third place in the Champions League standings with 10 points from four matches, having recorded three victories and one draw. Their most recent European outing ended in a 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague.
​
Dortmund are 12th with nine points, having won three of their four fixtures. Kovac's men defeated Real Betis 2-1 in their previous Champions League match.
​
The German side have also climbed to the top of the Bundesliga, establishing a two-point advantage over Bayern Munich. They have won three consecutive matches and remain unbeaten since their defeat to Bodø/Glimt in October.
​
